issue_families.name: Missing or regressed database indexes
issue_families.summary: A migration, table rebuild or new access pattern leaves a hot query without a usable index, so dashboard loads, filters or drill-downs fall back to full scans and become slow as the customer's tables grow.
issue_families.boundary_note: The data and visuals are correct and nothing fails outright; the only problem is latency caused by query execution, so it is perf rather than render or data_quality.

issue_families.name: Query result cache misses and invalidation storms
issue_families.summary: Cache keys that are too granular, invalidation that fires on every small write, or a cache that is cold after a deploy cause every viewer to hit the database, giving slow and inconsistent load times.
issue_families.boundary_note: When a cache returns wrong or stale content it is render; here the cache returns correct data but too rarely, so the symptom is purely speed.

issue_families.name: Report and export job queue backlog
issue_families.summary: Shared worker pools for scheduled reports and large exports get blocked by oversized jobs, peak-hour bursts or retries, so deliveries arrive hours late even though each file is eventually correct.
issue_families.boundary_note: Wrong export contents or failed delivery addresses are export; lateness caused by queue capacity and contention is perf.

issue_families.name: Browser-side slowness with very large result sets
issue_families.summary: Tables, pivots and charts that send tens of thousands of rows or points to the browser freeze the tab, scroll slowly or trigger 'page unresponsive' warnings, while the server query itself is quick.
issue_families.boundary_note: The visual is eventually drawn correctly; the issue is client CPU and memory cost, so it is perf rather than render.

issue_families.name: High-cardinality grouping and unbounded queries
issue_families.summary: Grouping by dimensions with hundreds of thousands of values, or queries with no date bound, produce enormous intermediate results that time out or exhaust query memory.
issue_families.boundary_note: Timeouts here come from query load and data volume rather than wrong calculations (data_quality) or API contract errors (api).

issue_families.name: Tenant query concurrency limits and shared compute contention
issue_families.summary: Per-workspace concurrency slots or shared compute pools are saturated by scheduled jobs, bulk refreshes or a neighbouring heavy workload, so interactive queries wait in a queue with 'waiting for capacity' messages.
issue_families.boundary_note: Requests are queued for capacity rather than rejected for quota (api rate limits) or permission (perm).

issue_families.name: Rollup and precomputation refresh overruns
issue_families.summary: Nightly rollup tables or pre-aggregated cubes take longer than their window after data growth or a backfill, so business-hours queries fall back to raw tables or wait on refresh locks.
issue_families.boundary_note: The ingestion itself completed (not sync) and the rolled-up values are correct (not data_quality); the problem is how long the precomputation runs and what it slows down.

issue_families.name: Expensive calculated fields and custom formulas
issue_families.summary: Customer-defined calculated metrics using nested lookups, regex matching, per-row date parsing or running totals over unbounded windows are evaluated row by row at query time and slow dashboards drastically.
issue_families.boundary_note: The formula results are correct; when a formula returns wrong numbers it is data_quality, but when it only costs time it is perf.

issue_families.name: Dashboard auto-refresh and widget fan-out overload
issue_families.summary: Very short auto-refresh intervals, dozens of widgets per dashboard and many open screens multiply query volume until the workspace's own refreshes slow everything down.
issue_families.boundary_note: This is load generated by the product's own dashboard behaviour, not a display defect (render) or an API client exceeding limits (api).

issue_families.name: Slow filter value lists, search and autocomplete
issue_families.summary: Filter dropdowns, global search and autocomplete fields scan full dimension tables or unindexed text on every keystroke, so pickers take many seconds to populate.
issue_families.boundary_note: Filters that apply the wrong values are render; pickers that are merely slow to populate are perf.

issue_families.name: Stale table statistics and bad query plans
issue_families.summary: After a large backfill, purge or bulk import, table statistics no longer reflect reality and the query planner picks nested loops or wrong join orders, making previously fast queries slow overnight.
issue_families.boundary_note: Indexes exist and data is correct; the plan choice under changed data volume is a performance problem rather than a sync or data_quality one.

issue_families.name: Memory growth in long-running browser sessions
issue_families.summary: Dashboards left open for hours on wall displays or kiosk screens accumulate chart instances, listeners or cached responses with every refresh until the browser becomes sluggish or crashes.
issue_families.boundary_note: The dashboard renders correctly at first and degrades only over time because of resource growth, which is perf rather than render.

issue_families.name: Oversized page payloads and uncached static assets
issue_families.summary: Dashboard definitions bloated with embedded images or history, or front-end assets served without long-lived cache headers, make every page open download megabytes before anything appears.
issue_families.boundary_note: Pages load slowly but successfully over a working network; blocked or unreachable hosts would be connectivity.

related_groups.shared_root_cause: After the orders table moved to automatic monthly partitions, newly created partitions were missing the (store_id, order_date) index, so any query touching recent months scanned those partitions fully while older months stayed fast.
The widget result cache key included the viewer's session identifier, so identical queries from different users and new sessions never reused a cached result.
The shared report worker pool processed jobs strictly first-in-first-out, so a single multi-hour full-history export blocked every smaller scheduled report queued behind it.
Scheduled report renders and interactive dashboard queries drew from the same per-workspace concurrency slots, so a burst of reports scheduled at the top of the hour starved interactive users.
A multi-year historical backfill made the nightly rollup refresh rebuild every partition instead of only changed ones, pushing the refresh into business hours.
Table statistics were not refreshed after a bulk import of several years of history, so the planner kept estimating tiny row counts and chose nested-loop joins.
The chart component created a new tooltip and resize listener on every auto-refresh without disposing of the previous ones, so memory grew steadily on screens left open.
Dashboards configured with a 30-second auto-refresh kept re-running every widget query even when the browser tab was hidden, multiplying load across many open screens.

tickets.subject: Store sales dashboard slow only for the current quarter
tickets.description: Customer reports the store sales dashboard loads in about 3 seconds when they pick last year, but anything that includes the current quarter takes 35-45 seconds.
tickets.resolution_notes: Since the orders table moved to automatic monthly partitions, the partitions created for the current quarter had been built without the (store_id, order_date) index, so recent months were scanned in full. Created the missing index on the affected partitions and fixed the partition template so new partitions inherit it. The current-quarter view now loads in under 4 seconds.

tickets.subject: 'Last 7 days' filter much slower than 'Last year'
tickets.description: The customer's analyst noticed something odd: filtering the order explorer to the last 7 days takes far longer than filtering to all of last year, even though it returns a fraction of the rows.
tickets.resolution_notes: The query plan showed full scans on the two newest monthly partitions, which had been created without the store and date index after the partitioning change; older partitions still had it, which explained why the larger historical range was faster. Added the index to all partitions created since the change and added a nightly check that every partition carries the expected indexes. The 7-day filter now returns in about a second.

tickets.subject: Month-to-date KPI tiles time out at the start of each month
tickets.description: Customer says the month-to-date revenue and units tiles on their executive board started timing out with 'Query exceeded 60s' at the beginning of this month. Prior-month tiles on the same board are fine.
tickets.resolution_notes: The new month's partition had been auto-created on a database shard where the earlier partition template correction had not yet been applied, so it lacked the (store_id, order_date) index and month-to-date queries hit an unindexed partition that grew all day. Added the index online and applied the corrected template to the remaining shards. Confirmed the MTD tiles load in about 2 seconds and verified next month's pre-created partition already has the index.

tickets.subject: Order line drill-down takes 20+ seconds
tickets.description: Clicking an order in the new order detail drill-down shows a spinner for 20-25 seconds before the line items appear. The order list itself is fast.
tickets.resolution_notes: The drill-down introduced a lookup of line items by order_id, but the line items table had no index on that foreign key, so each click scanned roughly 90 million rows for this customer. Added an index on order_id and confirmed drill-downs open in under a second for the customer's largest orders.

tickets.subject: Customer lookup by email is very slow
tickets.description: Agent summary: support staff at a pet supply retailer search shopper profiles by email in the Customer 360 page and each search takes 15-30 seconds. Searching by shopper ID is instant.
tickets.resolution_notes: Email search wrapped the column in a lower-case function to make matching case-insensitive, which prevented the existing email index from being used. Added an expression index on the lower-cased email and confirmed email lookups now return in about 200 ms with the same results as before.

tickets.subject: Filtering by custom 'region code' attribute is slow
tickets.description: Since the customer started using a custom attribute called region code as a dashboard filter, every widget on their inventory movement dashboard takes 10+ seconds to refresh when the filter is applied.
tickets.resolution_notes: Custom attributes are stored in a flexible attribute column that is not indexed, so filtering on region code inspected every row. Promoted region code to a dedicated indexed column for the workspace and backfilled it. Filtered refreshes now complete in 1-2 seconds; documented that heavily filtered custom attributes can be promoted on request.

tickets.subject: Dashboard only fast on the second view
tickets.description: Customer says the merchandising dashboard takes about 25 seconds for each person the first time they open it, then loads instantly if they reload. Colleagues opening it a minute later still wait the full time.
tickets.resolution_notes: The widget result cache key included the viewer's session identifier, so cached results were never shared between users or across new sessions. Removed the session component from the key while keeping the row-level permission scope in it so users only share results they are allowed to see; the change was enabled for this customer's workspace first. A second user now gets cached results in under 2 seconds.

tickets.subject: Morning stand-up board slow for every regional manager
tickets.description: About 40 regional managers open the same daily KPI board at 8:00 for a stand-up call. The customer's admin reports that every one of them waits around 20 seconds, which makes the call start late each day.
tickets.resolution_notes: Each manager's request produced a distinct cache entry because the cache key incorporated the session ID, so 40 identical queries ran at once. Rolled the corrected cache key, built from the query fingerprint plus the user's permission scope instead of the session, out to all workspaces. During the next stand-up only the first request ran a query and the remaining managers loaded the board in 1-2 seconds.

tickets.subject: Embedded dashboard in partner portal slow for every visitor
tickets.description: The customer embeds a supplier scorecard in their partner portal. Suppliers report it takes 15-20 seconds to appear on each visit, while the same dashboard opened directly in the app feels quicker for internal staff.
tickets.resolution_notes: Embedded views create a fresh short-lived session for each visit, and the embed rendering path built its own result cache key that still included the session ID, so embedded traffic never got a cache hit. Changed that key to the query fingerprint and the embed's permission scope. Embedded loads dropped to around 2 seconds after the first visitor of each supplier scope.

tickets.classification_rationale: Data arrives correctly and on time, so this is not sync; the problem is that each arrival wipes the cache and slows queries.
tickets.subject: Dashboards never seem to use the cache
tickets.description: The customer's operations team says their dashboards always behave like a cold load, 10-15 seconds per view, all day long. Their connected point-of-sale source sends small updates every two minutes.
tickets.resolution_notes: Every incoming micro-batch invalidated the entire workspace cache rather than only the datasets that changed, so the cache was cleared roughly every two minutes. Scoped invalidation to the affected dataset and added a 5-minute minimum freshness window, which the customer agreed to. Cache hit rate rose from under 5% to about 80% and typical loads are now under 3 seconds.

tickets.subject: Slow Monday mornings after weekend maintenance
tickets.description: Customer reports that the first hour of every Monday is painfully slow across all dashboards; by mid-morning everything is normal again.
tickets.resolution_notes: Weekend maintenance restarts cleared the in-memory result cache, so Monday's first wave of users all hit the database cold. As a workaround we enabled a scheduled warm-up that pre-runs the customer's 20 most-viewed dashboards after maintenance; a persistent cache tier that survives restarts is scheduled for a later release. The following Monday's first-hour load times matched the rest of the week.

tickets.subject: One large table widget always re-runs its query
tickets.description: Everything on the customer's assortment dashboard loads from cache quickly except the SKU detail table, which takes 18 seconds every single time.
tickets.resolution_notes: The SKU table result was about 9 MB, above the cache's 5 MB per-entry limit, so the cache silently skipped storing it. Switched the widget to server-side pagination so each cached page is small, and added a log warning when an entry exceeds the limit. The table now loads its first page in about a second.

tickets.classification_rationale: The report content and recipients were correct and it was eventually delivered; the delay came from queue capacity, so it is perf rather than export.
tickets.subject: Monday sales report arrived almost five hours late
tickets.description: Customer's 7:00 weekly sales report did not land in inboxes until 11:40. They rely on it for a 9:00 meeting and want to know why it was delayed.
tickets.resolution_notes: A full-history export from another workspace had been running for over four hours on the shared report worker pool, and because jobs were processed strictly in arrival order, every scheduled report behind it waited. A separate pool for long-running exports, together with per-workspace fair scheduling, went live on 18 June. The following Monday the report was delivered at 7:03.

tickets.subject: Month-end PDF board pack delayed
tickets.description: The customer's finance lead says the board pack PDF that normally arrives at 6:00 on the first business day came after lunch this month.
tickets.resolution_notes: The board pack job was queued behind a very large ad-hoc export that occupied workers for hours, since the queue had no separation between short scheduled jobs and long exports. As an immediate workaround we moved the board pack to the front of the queue and it was delivered at 13:10; engineering started work on a dedicated pool for long exports with a per-workspace share of workers. Verified the following month-end board pack, after that change shipped, arrived at 6:02.

tickets.subject: Small CSV export stuck on 'Queued' for hours
tickets.description: Customer requested a 2,000-row CSV export at 10:15 and the export panel still said 'Queued' at 13:30. Nothing appeared to be wrong with the export settings.
tickets.resolution_notes: Their tiny export was waiting behind an exceptionally large full-history export on the shared first-in-first-out queue. Released the stuck job by moving it ahead of the large export while the planned separate lane for large exports was still being built. Once started, the 2,000-row export completed in under a minute.

tickets.subject: Report backlog grows while workers look idle
tickets.description: Customer escalated that multiple scheduled reports were 1-2 hours late on Tuesday morning. Our status page showed no incident.
tickets.resolution_notes: The report renderer autoscaled on CPU usage, but workers were mostly waiting on database queries, so CPU stayed low and the autoscaler removed capacity while the queue kept growing. Changed scaling to use queue depth and oldest-job age. Queue age stayed under 5 minutes through the next peak and the customer's reports arrived on time.

tickets.subject: Reports due at 9:00 sharp arrive between 9:20 and 10:00
tickets.description: Customer schedules dozens of store reports for exactly 09:00 local time and says they trickle in over the next hour instead of arriving together.
tickets.resolution_notes: Many workspaces in the same time zone scheduled reports at exactly 09:00, creating a burst far above sustained capacity at that minute. Added pre-emptive scale-up ahead of known schedule peaks and began rendering data for fixed-time reports a few minutes early so delivery happens at the scheduled time. The customer's 09:00 reports now all arrive by 09:04.

tickets.subject: Oversized annual export keeps restarting and slowing other reports
tickets.description: A customer's analyst scheduled an export of all line items for three years. It never completes, and other reports for the workspace have been late since it was created.
tickets.resolution_notes: The export hit the 60-minute worker time limit and was automatically re-queued, running three times per night and occupying a worker each time. As an immediate workaround we split it into twelve monthly exports that each finish within the limit; a permanent change to cap automatic retries for timed-out jobs is scheduled. The other reports were back on time the next morning.

tickets.subject: Pivot table freezes browser tab
tickets.description: When the customer expands all rows on a pivot of sales by store and SKU (about 80,000 rows), the browser tab freezes for close to a minute. The request itself shows complete in the network panel after about a second.
tickets.resolution_notes: The pivot component rendered every row into the page at once rather than only the visible rows. Enabled row virtualization for pivots above 1,000 rows. Expanding all rows now responds in under 2 seconds and scrolling is smooth.

tickets.classification_rationale: The chart eventually draws correctly; the browser stalls because of the point volume, so this is perf rather than render.
tickets.subject: 'Page unresponsive' warning on per-minute traffic chart
tickets.description: Customer gets the browser's 'Page unresponsive' prompt when opening a line chart of per-minute footfall for a full year. Shorter ranges work.
tickets.resolution_notes: A year of per-minute data sent roughly 525,000 points per series to the browser. Enabled server-side downsampling that keeps the visual shape while sending at most 2,000 points per series, with full resolution returned when the user zooms in. The full-year chart now opens in about 2 seconds without the warning.

tickets.subject: Hovering over SKU scatter plot is laggy
tickets.description: Customer plots margin against sell-through for all 120k SKUs. The chart appears quickly, but moving the mouse across it stutters and tooltips lag several seconds behind the cursor.
tickets.resolution_notes: The scatter plot used vector rendering and checked every point on each mouse move to find the nearest one for the tooltip. Switched large scatter plots to canvas rendering with a spatial index for hover lookups. Tooltips now follow the cursor without visible lag.

tickets.subject: Sorting a large table takes ~10 seconds per click
tickets.description: Customer says each click on a column header in their 60,000-row stock table locks the page for about ten seconds before the new order appears.
tickets.resolution_notes: Tables below an outdated size threshold were sorted in the browser, and the threshold had been set far too high, so 60,000 rows were sorted client-side with a slow comparison for mixed text and numbers. Lowered the threshold so large tables sort on the server and return only the visible page. Header sorts now complete in under a second.

tickets.subject: Store manager tablet app hangs on product list
tickets.description: Store managers using the tablet app say opening the product performance list hangs the app for 30+ seconds and sometimes closes it. The same list in the web app is fine.
tickets.resolution_notes: The tablet app requested the full product list for the store in one response and built every row in memory, which older tablets could not handle. As a workaround, managers were pointed to the category summary view; the next app release added paged loading of 200 rows at a time. After updating, the list opened in about 2 seconds on the customer's oldest tablet model.

tickets.subject: Store map lags when panning
tickets.description: The customer's store map shows about 30,000 pickup points. Dragging or zooming the map stutters badly and sometimes takes a few seconds to catch up.
tickets.resolution_notes: Every marker was drawn individually and redrawn on each pan event. Enabled marker clustering for maps with more than 2,000 points and throttled redraws during drag. Panning and zooming are now smooth, with individual markers shown once the user zooms in to a city level.

tickets.subject: 'Query exceeded memory limit' grouping by store and SKU
tickets.description: Customer's category manager built a table grouped by store and SKU for the full year and gets 'Query exceeded memory limit (code Q-MEM-02)' every time it runs.
tickets.resolution_notes: Store by SKU for this customer produced about 14 million groups, which exceeded the per-query memory budget before sorting. Changed the widget to a top 500 by revenue with an 'all other' row and provided a scheduled export for the full breakdown. The widget now loads in about 5 seconds and the full detail arrives as a nightly file.

tickets.subject: Shared exploration defaults to 'All time' and crawls
tickets.description: A saved exploration that the whole buying team uses takes over a minute to open. The customer noticed the date picker on it says 'All time'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The exploration had been saved without a date bound, so every open scanned eight years of transactions. Set its default to the last 13 months with the option to widen it, and added a warning when someone saves a shared exploration with an unbounded range. It now opens in about 4 seconds.

tickets.classification_rationale: The unique shopper count was correct but took minutes to compute; an incorrect count would be data_quality.
tickets.subject: Unique shopper count tile takes minutes
tickets.description: Customer reports the 'unique shoppers, last 3 years' tile is so slow that it often hits the 120-second limit. Other tiles on the board are quick.
tickets.resolution_notes: The tile performed an exact distinct count across roughly 900 million transactions. With the customer's agreement switched it to the approximate distinct count option (typically within 1%), with an exact recount available as a scheduled job. The tile now loads in about 3 seconds and the nightly exact figure matched the approximation within 0.4%.

tickets.subject: Promotion impact dashboard times out
tickets.description: The promotion impact dashboard joins promotions to products and has started timing out since the customer loaded their new loyalty campaign, which applies to thousands of products.
tickets.resolution_notes: Promotions and products are many-to-many, and the query joined both sides at line level before aggregating, creating around 2 billion intermediate rows; results were de-duplicated correctly but very slowly. Rewrote the model to aggregate through the promotion-product bridge before joining sales. The dashboard loads in 6 seconds and spot-checked totals were unchanged.

tickets.classification_rationale: The query API accepted the request as documented; the 504 came from the size of the result being computed, so it sits in perf rather than api.
tickets.subject: Query API returns 504 when grouping by transaction
tickets.description: Customer's internal script calls the query endpoint with group_by=transaction_id for a quarter and receives HTTP 504 after 120 seconds. The same call grouped by day works.
tickets.resolution_notes: Grouping by transaction ID returned one group per transaction (about 40 million), which is row-level extraction rather than aggregation and exceeded the query time budget. Advised the customer to use the bulk export job for row-level data and kept their dashboards on daily grouping. Their script now finishes the quarterly extract in about 12 minutes through the export job.

tickets.subject: Cohort retention chart never finishes
tickets.description: Customer opened the cohort retention template with weekly cohorts from their first year of trading. The chart spins until it shows 'Query timed out'.
tickets.resolution_notes: Weekly cohorts over five years created a cohort-by-week matrix of roughly 68,000 cells, each needing a self-join on shopper history. Limited the default to the most recent 104 weekly cohorts, offered monthly cohorts for longer history, and added a nightly precomputed cohort table. The chart now renders in about 7 seconds.

tickets.subject: 'Waiting for capacity' message at 9:00 on Mondays
tickets.description: Customer reports that at 9:00 every Monday their dashboards show 'Waiting for capacity...' for one to three minutes before loading.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer has about 150 reports scheduled for 9:00 on Mondays, and scheduled renders shared the same workspace concurrency slots as people opening dashboards. Reserved a portion of slots for interactive queries so scheduled work can no longer take all of them. Next Monday interactive waits stayed under 5 seconds while reports still completed by 9:12.

tickets.classification_rationale: The spinner resembles a render loading failure, but every widget eventually loaded and the delay was queueing for capacity, so it is perf.
tickets.subject: Every dashboard spins for two minutes right on the hour
tickets.description: The customer's admin noticed that at the top of each hour, every dashboard in the workspace sits on a spinner for around two minutes, then loads normally. Between hours there is no problem.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's hourly store reports all ran at :00 and consumed every concurrency slot in the workspace, so interactive queries queued behind them. Separated scheduled and interactive workloads with reserved slots and spread the hourly reports across the first ten minutes. Monitored three hourly cycles and saw no interactive queuing.

tickets.subject: Early-shift users get 'queue wait exceeded' errors
tickets.description: Store supervisors starting at 6:00 see 'Query cancelled: queue wait exceeded 90s' on the opening checklist dashboard. By 6:15 it works.
tickets.resolution_notes: 120 store-opening reports were scheduled for 6:00 and occupied all workspace query slots, so the supervisors' interactive queries waited past the 90-second queue limit. Reserved interactive capacity and moved the opening reports to start at 5:45 with the customer's approval. Supervisors loaded the checklist without errors the following morning.

tickets.subject: Slow dashboards every afternoon with no change in usage
tickets.description: Customer reports dashboards become two to three times slower between roughly 14:00 and 15:30 each weekday. Their own usage and data volume are flat across the day.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's workspace shared a compute pool with another tenant whose large daily batch analysis started at 14:00, saturating shared CPU. Moved the customer to a less contended pool and tightened per-tenant CPU limits on shared pools. Afternoon load times now match the morning baseline.

tickets.subject: Analyst explorations slowing store dashboards
tickets.description: Customer says store staff dashboards become very slow whenever the central analytics team is running ad-hoc explorations, usually mid-morning.
tickets.resolution_notes: Ten analysts each running heavy multi-year explorations consumed all of the workspace's concurrency slots, leaving store dashboards waiting. Configured workload classes so dashboards keep reserved slots and ad-hoc explorations queue among themselves. Store dashboards stayed under 4 seconds during the next analytics session.

tickets.subject: Leaving a slow dashboard doesn't free anything up
tickets.description: Customer noticed that if a user gives up on a slow dashboard and opens another one, the second one is also slow, as if the first is still running in the background.
tickets.resolution_notes: Widget queries were not cancelled when users navigated away, so abandoned queries kept occupying concurrency slots until they finished. Added cancellation of in-flight widget queries on navigation and tab close. Query logs confirmed abandoned queries now stop within a second and slot usage dropped about 30% at peak.

tickets.classification_rationale: The backfilled data loaded successfully and totals are correct; only query speed suffered while rollups rebuilt, so perf rather than sync.
tickets.subject: Dashboards slow until late morning since history backfill
tickets.description: Since the customer loaded six years of historical sales last week, their dashboards are slow every morning until about 11:00, then fast for the rest of the day.
tickets.resolution_notes: After the backfill the nightly rollup refresh rebuilt every historical partition instead of only changed ones, so it ran until late morning and dashboards fell back to raw tables meanwhile. Corrected change tracking so only modified partitions are rebuilt. The refresh now finishes by 3:30 and morning dashboards use rollups again.

tickets.subject: 'Aggregates updating' banner still showing at 10am
tickets.description: Customer sees a yellow 'Aggregates updating - results may be slower' banner on all dashboards until about 10:00 each day. It used to clear before anyone logged in.
tickets.resolution_notes: The aggregate refresh had started reprocessing all partitions every night after a multi-year history import marked them as modified. Reset the partition change markers and confirmed only new days are refreshed. The banner now clears at about 2:45, well before business hours.

tickets.subject: 8:00 scheduled reports now take 20 minutes to generate
tickets.description: Customer noticed their 8:00 regional reports, which used to arrive by 8:02, now arrive around 8:20. Nothing changed in the report definitions.
tickets.resolution_notes: The reports were querying raw tables because the nightly rollup refresh was still running, a consequence of the recent historical backfill causing full rebuilds of every partition. Fixed partition change detection so the refresh is incremental again. Reports returned to arriving by 8:02 the next day.

tickets.subject: Dashboards freeze for ~15 minutes around 4:00
tickets.description: A customer with staff in another time zone reports dashboards hang for about 15 minutes at 4:00 our platform time every day, then recover.
tickets.resolution_notes: The rollup refresh replaced the summary table in place and held an exclusive lock during the swap, so queries waited until it finished. Changed the refresh to build into a shadow table and switch over atomically. Dashboards now stay responsive throughout the refresh.

tickets.subject: Adding 'channel' breakdown made the sales board slow
tickets.description: Customer added a breakdown by sales channel (store, web, marketplace) to their sales board and it went from loading in 2 seconds to around 25 seconds.
tickets.resolution_notes: The pre-aggregated rollup did not include the channel dimension, so any widget split by channel bypassed the rollup and queried raw transactions. Added channel to the rollup definition and rebuilt it. The board with the channel breakdown now loads in about 2 seconds.

tickets.classification_rationale: Late returns were ingested correctly; the problem was the cost of repeatedly recomputing old periods, so this is perf rather than sync.
tickets.subject: Hourly refresh falling behind, slower dashboards all afternoon
tickets.description: Customer's hourly incremental refresh has been taking longer than an hour since they started importing late returns, so refreshes overlap and dashboards are slow most afternoons.
tickets.resolution_notes: Each late-arriving return caused the hourly refresh to recompute 30 days of aggregates, so refreshes overlapped. As a workaround, limited the hourly lookback to 7 days and added a nightly full recompute of the last 30 days; a smarter refresh that only recomputes affected days is scheduled for a future release. Hourly refreshes now complete in about 12 minutes.

tickets.subject: Size breakdown widget slow after adding regex calculated field
tickets.description: Customer created a calculated field that pulls the garment size out of the product name with a regular expression. Any widget using it takes 30+ seconds.
tickets.resolution_notes: The regex was evaluated on every transaction row at query time, roughly 200 million evaluations per load. Materialized the extracted size as a derived product attribute computed once when products are loaded, and pointed the widgets at it. The values were identical and the widgets now load in about 2 seconds.

tickets.subject: Margin % metric makes the whole board slow
tickets.description: The customer's finance analyst says the gross margin dashboard became sluggish (15-20 seconds) after they defined a margin % metric that looks up unit cost for each sale.
tickets.resolution_notes: The metric used the per-row LOOKUP function against the cost table, which executes as a separate lookup for each sale. Rewrote the metric to use a modelled join between sales and the cost table, giving the same results. The dashboard now loads in 3 seconds.

tickets.subject: Cumulative revenue chart gets slower every week
tickets.description: Customer reports that a daily chart of cumulative revenue keeps getting slower; it took 2 seconds at launch and now takes close to 30.
tickets.resolution_notes: The running total was defined over all history with no partition, so every point recomputed the sum from the first sale, and cost grew with the data. Changed it to a year-to-date running total partitioned by fiscal year, which matches how the chart is used, and added a precomputed cumulative column for the all-time variant. The chart loads in under 2 seconds.

tickets.classification_rationale: The parsed dates were correct, so this is not data_quality; parsing text on every query only made the dashboard slow.
tickets.subject: Dashboards using 'delivery date' field load slowly
tickets.description: Customer's delivery date arrives as text (DD/MM/YYYY) and they built a calculated field to convert it. Widgets that filter on that field take around 20 seconds.
tickets.resolution_notes: The conversion was parsed on every row and every query, and filtering on a parsed value prevented any index use. Added a typed date column populated during load from the same parsing rule, and switched the widgets to it. Spot checks showed the same dates and the widgets now load in about a second.

tickets.subject: Deeply nested calculated metrics time out
tickets.description: Agent summary: a customer's 'contribution margin after returns' metric is built from five other calculated metrics, each built on others. The KPI tile using it now times out after 60 seconds.
tickets.resolution_notes: The nested definitions expanded into a query that recomputed the same intermediate subtotals many times. Flattened the metric chain into a single definition and enabled reuse of shared subexpressions. The tile returns the same value in 4 seconds; we also documented the recommended nesting depth for calculated metrics.

tickets.subject: Region field with huge CASE statement slows every widget
tickets.description: Customer maps 600 store codes to regions using one long CASE expression in a calculated field. Every widget split by region is slow.
tickets.resolution_notes: The 600-branch expression was evaluated sequentially for every row. Replaced it with a small store-to-region mapping table joined to sales, which the customer can now edit directly. Region widgets went from about 18 seconds to under 2, with identical regional totals.

tickets.subject: Workspace slows down when the operations centre is staffed
tickets.description: Customer says the whole workspace gets noticeably slower during operations centre shifts. The ops centre has 25 screens each showing a dashboard.
tickets.resolution_notes: Each ops screen was set to auto-refresh every 30 seconds and refreshed all widgets regardless of whether the data had changed, generating thousands of queries per hour. Raised the minimum refresh interval to 2 minutes for those dashboards and enabled refresh-only-when-data-changed. Workspace query volume dropped by about 75% and other users' load times returned to normal.

tickets.subject: Usage page shows 2 million queries a day for 40 users
tickets.description: The customer's admin noticed in the usage page that the workspace runs roughly 2 million queries per day even though only about 40 people use it, and dashboards have felt slower lately.
tickets.resolution_notes: Several dashboards had a 30-second auto-refresh and were left open in background tabs, which kept refreshing even when nobody was looking. Changed the product to pause auto-refresh when the tab is hidden and resume on focus, and raised the refresh interval on those dashboards. Daily queries fell to around 300,000 and dashboard latency improved.

tickets.subject: Slow dashboards even though nobody is using them
tickets.description: Customer is puzzled: overnight, when no staff are working, monitoring shows query load on their workspace stays high, and the first people in each morning find dashboards slow.
tickets.resolution_notes: A dozen browser tabs on office machines had been left open with 30-second auto-refresh, so dashboards kept refreshing all night while hidden. Enabled pausing of auto-refresh for hidden tabs and set a 2-minute minimum interval. Overnight query load dropped to near zero and morning load times were normal.

tickets.subject: 70-widget dashboard loads in waves
tickets.description: Customer's all-in-one regional dashboard has about 70 widgets. They load a few at a time over 40 seconds, top to bottom.
tickets.resolution_notes: Each widget made its own request and the browser allows only a handful of parallel connections per host, so widgets queued in the browser. Enabled batched widget queries so the dashboard sends a few combined requests, and suggested splitting the board into tabs that load on demand. The board now completes in about 9 seconds.

tickets.subject: Same query runs twelve times on one dashboard
tickets.description: Agent summary: query logs for a customer's category dashboard show the identical sales-by-week query executing twelve times per page load, once for each chart that visualises it differently.
tickets.resolution_notes: Widgets sharing the same underlying query were not deduplicated within a page load. Enabled per-load query deduplication so widgets with an identical query fingerprint share one execution. The dashboard now issues one query instead of twelve and loads about four times faster.

tickets.subject: Clicking a bar to cross-filter takes 15 seconds
tickets.description: When the customer clicks a region bar to cross-filter their dashboard, everything grays out for 15 seconds, including widgets that don't use region at all.
tickets.resolution_notes: Cross-filter clicks refreshed all 40 widgets on the dashboard, even those not linked to the region field. Changed cross-filtering to refresh only widgets connected to the clicked field. A cross-filter click now updates the eight relevant widgets in about 2 seconds.

tickets.subject: Store filter dropdown takes 12 seconds to open
tickets.description: Customer reports the store filter on every dashboard shows 'Loading values...' for about 12 seconds before the list of stores appears.
tickets.resolution_notes: The filter built its value list by selecting distinct store names from the transactions table instead of from the store dimension. Switched the filter source to the dimension table. The dropdown now opens in under half a second with the same list of stores.

tickets.subject: Product autocomplete lags while typing
tickets.description: Customer says typing in the product search box is painful: each letter takes a second or two to appear and suggestions jump around.
tickets.resolution_notes: Autocomplete sent a query on every keystroke using a leading-wildcard match, which could not use an index on product names. Added a 250 ms debounce and a trigram index for substring matches. Suggestions now appear within about 200 ms of the user pausing.

tickets.classification_rationale: Results were correct and permission checks were not wrong, only slow, so this is perf rather than perm.
tickets.subject: Dashboard catalogue search takes 20 seconds
tickets.description: In a workspace with about 9,000 dashboards, searching the catalogue for a title takes around 20 seconds. Admins get results noticeably faster than regular members.
tickets.resolution_notes: The search checked view permission separately for each candidate result, issuing thousands of permission lookups for members (admins skip the check). Replaced this with a single batched permission evaluation per search. Members now get correct results in under a second.

tickets.subject: City filter slow after choosing a region
tickets.description: Customer has cascading filters: region then city. Choosing a region makes the city list take 8-10 seconds to update.
tickets.resolution_notes: The city filter had 'only show values with data in the selected period' enabled, which ran a query over transactions each time the region changed. With the customer's agreement, switched the city list to use the location hierarchy instead. The city list now updates instantly; cities with no sales in the period simply show no data when selected.

tickets.subject: Saved views menu takes ages to open
tickets.description: Customer reports that the 'Saved views' menu on the sales dashboard takes 10+ seconds to open for one service user and freezes briefly for everyone else.
tickets.resolution_notes: An internal script at the customer had been creating a new saved view on every run, leaving over 3,000 near-identical saved views, and the menu loaded all of them at once. Helped the customer remove the redundant views and fix their script, and added pagination to the menu. The menu now opens immediately.

tickets.subject: Tablet app product search very slow in stores
tickets.description: Store staff using the tablet app say product search takes 20-30 seconds on first use each day. Searching the same products on the web app is quick.
tickets.resolution_notes: The tablet app downloaded the full product catalogue (about 40 MB) to search locally, and the cached copy was discarded daily. Switched the app to the server-side product search endpoint, keeping a small cache of recent results. First searches now return in about a second on store Wi-Fi.

tickets.classification_rationale: The imported history is complete and correct; only query planning was affected, so this is perf rather than sync.
tickets.subject: Basket analysis went from seconds to minutes overnight
tickets.description: Customer imported four years of historical transactions on Friday. From Monday, the basket analysis report takes about three minutes instead of five seconds.
tickets.resolution_notes: Table statistics had not been refreshed after the bulk import, so the planner still assumed the transactions table was small and chose nested-loop joins. Ran a statistics refresh on the affected tables and confirmed the planner switched to hash joins. The report loads in 5 seconds again.

tickets.subject: Store comparison widget slow right after onboarding migration
tickets.description: A newly onboarded retailer says the store comparison widget was quick during their trial but became very slow the day their historical data migration finished.
tickets.resolution_notes: The migration bulk-loaded several years of history without triggering a statistics update, so row estimates were off by a factor of thousands and the planner chose a poor join order. Refreshed statistics and added an automatic statistics update at the end of every bulk import. The widget now loads in about 3 seconds.

tickets.subject: Only reports involving loyalty members are slow
tickets.description: Customer notes that any report joining sales to the loyalty member list now crawls, while sales-only reports are unaffected. They recently loaded five years of member history.
tickets.resolution_notes: The member table's statistics still reflected the pre-import size, so the planner looped over it row by row when joining. Refreshed statistics for the member and sales tables and confirmed the improved plan. Loyalty reports dropped from around 70 seconds to 4.

tickets.subject: Queries got slower after we deleted most of our old data
tickets.description: Customer purged data older than two years to meet their retention policy, removing about 70% of rows, and expected dashboards to get faster. Instead several got slower.
tickets.resolution_notes: Statistics still described the pre-purge table, so the planner overestimated row counts and chose plans suited to a much larger table. Refreshed statistics and changed the automatic refresh trigger to fire on large deletes as well as inserts. Dashboards are now faster than before the purge.

tickets.subject: Filtering to the online store is slow, physical stores are fast
tickets.description: Customer reports that every dashboard filtered to their web store takes 20+ seconds, while filtering to any physical store is instant.
tickets.resolution_notes: The web store accounts for about 60% of transactions, but the planner used a uniform per-store estimate and chose an index lookup that suits small stores. Increased the statistics detail on the store column so the skew is captured, and the planner now uses a scan for the web store. Web store dashboards load in about 3 seconds.

tickets.subject: Gradual slowdown over several weeks
tickets.description: Customer says nothing changed on their side, but dashboards have been getting a little slower every week for about six weeks.
tickets.resolution_notes: Automatic statistics maintenance had been paused on the database shard hosting this customer during an earlier maintenance and was never re-enabled, so estimates drifted as data grew. Re-enabled it, refreshed statistics, and added an alert when automatic maintenance is off for more than a day. Load times returned to their level of two months earlier.

tickets.subject: Wall display browser crashes overnight
tickets.description: The customer runs the sales dashboard on a wall-mounted screen in their head office. Every morning the screen shows the browser's out-of-memory error page.
tickets.resolution_notes: Each auto-refresh created new chart tooltips and resize listeners without removing the old ones, so memory grew steadily until the browser ran out. Enabled the nightly page reload option for the display as a stopgap until the chart component fix, which disposes of previous instances on refresh, shipped on 30 July. After the fix a test screen stayed at a stable memory level for 72 hours.

tickets.subject: Dashboard gets slower the longer it stays open
tickets.description: Customer says if they leave the KPI dashboard open all day, hovering and scrolling become sluggish by afternoon. Reloading the page fixes it until the next day.
tickets.resolution_notes: Browser profiling showed thousands of detached chart tooltip elements and duplicate resize handlers, one set added per auto-refresh. The chart component patch released on 30 July cleans up handlers and tooltips when it re-renders. After the release, memory use stayed flat over a full working day.

tickets.subject: Back-office kiosk needs restarting every afternoon
tickets.description: Store back-office PCs show the stock dashboard in kiosk mode. Staff say by around 15:00 the PC is crawling and they restart it daily.
tickets.resolution_notes: The kiosk dashboard refreshed every 5 minutes and leaked chart tooltip and listener objects on each refresh, the same chart defect already under investigation. The cleanup fix that disposes of old instances was deployed on 30 July, and afterwards the kiosks ran a full trading day without slowing down.

tickets.subject: Live orders ticker freezes the tab after a few hours
tickets.description: Customer's e-commerce team keeps the live orders ticker open during promotions. After 3-4 hours the tab freezes and must be closed.
tickets.resolution_notes: The ticker kept every received order event in memory for the whole session, reaching hundreds of thousands of events during promotions. Changed it to keep only the most recent 500 events in a ring buffer, with older ones available through the order explorer. The ticker ran through a 10-hour promotion without issue.

tickets.subject: TV playlist mode becomes choppy after a day
tickets.description: Customer uses playlist mode to rotate eight dashboards on a screen every 60 seconds. Transitions are smooth at first but become choppy after about a day.
tickets.resolution_notes: Playlist mode kept every previously shown dashboard loaded in the background instead of unloading it on rotation. Changed it to unload dashboards when they rotate out and preload only the next one. Memory use is now constant across rotations and transitions stay smooth.

tickets.subject: Delivery map screen slows to a crawl by evening
tickets.description: A logistics team keeps a delivery map dashboard open all day. By evening panning is very slow and the browser uses several gigabytes of memory.
tickets.resolution_notes: The map widget cached every map tile it had ever fetched with no size limit. As an interim workaround we enabled the scheduled nightly reload option for that display; a bounded tile cache is scheduled for an upcoming release. With the nightly reload in place the screen stayed responsive through the next week.

tickets.subject: Dashboard with pasted images takes 30 seconds to open
tickets.description: The customer's marketing dashboard includes several text widgets with pasted campaign images. It takes about 30 seconds to open even before any charts start loading.
tickets.resolution_notes: Pasted images were stored inline in the dashboard definition, making it about 15 MB that had to download before rendering. Moved the images to asset storage and replaced them with references loaded lazily. The dashboard definition is now 40 KB and the page appears in under 2 seconds.

tickets.classification_rationale: Pages loaded successfully over a working network; the slowness came from missing cache headers on our assets, so this is perf rather than connectivity.
tickets.subject: Every page change feels like a first load since Tuesday
tickets.description: Several users at a customer report that since Tuesday, moving between dashboards takes 5-8 seconds of blank page each time, as if nothing is cached.
tickets.resolution_notes: Tuesday's release served front-end asset bundles without long-lived cache headers, so browsers re-downloaded about 6 MB of scripts on every navigation. Restored the correct cache headers for versioned assets. Repeat navigations now start rendering in under a second.

tickets.subject: Heavily edited dashboard opens slowly
tickets.description: Customer's main planning dashboard has been edited almost daily for two years and now takes around 12 seconds to open. A copy of it opens quickly.
tickets.resolution_notes: The dashboard response included its full revision history, around 500 versions, every time it was opened; the copy had no history, which is why it was fast. Changed history to load only when the version panel is opened. The original dashboard now opens as fast as the copy.

tickets.subject: Sales trend chart with annotations loads slowly
tickets.description: Customer's team annotates their daily sales chart with promotions and store events. The chart now takes 10 seconds to show up, and the customer suspects the annotations.
tickets.resolution_notes: All 12,000 annotations ever created for the chart were sent with every load, regardless of the date range shown. Changed annotations to load only for the visible range and fetch more as the user scrolls or zooms. The chart now appears in about a second.

tickets.subject: Widget editor slow to open in workspace with thousands of fields
tickets.description: In a workspace where teams have created around 4,000 custom fields, opening the widget editor takes 8-10 seconds every time.
tickets.resolution_notes: The editor downloaded the complete field catalogue, around 8 MB, on every open and did not reuse it between edits. Changed the catalogue to load on demand by folder, compressed it, and cached it in the browser with a version check. The editor now opens in about a second after the first use.

tickets.subject: Embedded store scorecard slow inside customer's intranet
tickets.description: Customer embeds a store scorecard in their intranet home page. Employees report the intranet now takes noticeably longer to finish loading, waiting on the embedded frame.
tickets.resolution_notes: Embeds loaded the full application bundle, including the dashboard editor, even though embedded viewers cannot edit. Switched embeds to the lightweight viewer bundle, cutting the download from about 5 MB to 900 KB. The embedded scorecard now appears in about 1.5 seconds.
